newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot natgas eases ahead of cooler weather.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot natgas eases ahead of cooler weather.

text.p: U.S. spot natural gas prices shed previous gains on Tuesday as forecasts called for a return of cooler weather by the weekend and extending into early next week, industry sources said.
Louisiana Gulf Coast prices slipped an average of three cents to about $2.12-2.17 per mmBtu, with Henry Hub quoted at $2.14-2.17.

In south Texas, cooling demand kept prices around $2.09-2.10, traders said. Temperatures in Houston were expected to reach highs of 91 and 93 degrees F on Wednesday and Thursday, respectively, according to Weather Services Corp.
In west Texas, Permian prices fell two cents to $1.94-1.96, while Waha values were quoted in the low-$2 area.
Southern California prices held at $2.14-2.15 as storage demand counteracted cooler-than-normal weather in southern California, traders said.
In the Midwest, prices eased by one to two cents to about $2.00-2.02, with Chicago city-gate quoted in the high-teens to low-$2.20s.
Temperatures in the region are forecast to average five to 15 degrees F above normal Wednesday but then turn gradually cooler into the weekend and early next week, WSC reported.
In the East, New York city gate prices also slipped a few cents to the low-$2.40s despite temperature highs around 90 degrees F expected to last through Friday.
According to WSC, temperatures in the Northeast are expected to return to near normal by the weekend.
Separately, injection estimates for Wednesday's American Gas Association storage report have ranged from 85 to 110 bcf, versus a gain of 88 bcf a year ago.
